blocks.x: Key definitions
Print Area The specific range of cells selected to be printed, set from the Page Setup dialog's Sheet tab. Excel automatically creates a named range called Print_Area for it.

Page Break A divider that splits a worksheet into separate pages for printing. Breaks can be automatic (inserted by the program based on paper size and margins) or manual (inserted by the user at a chosen row or column).
Page Break Preview A view mode (View > Page Break Preview) that shows exactly where each page will end, with blue lines marking the breaks, letting you drag them to adjust before printing.
Print Titles Rows or columns that repeat on every printed page — for example a header row of column labels — set in the Sheet tab so multi-page printouts stay readable.

Scaling (Adjust To / Fit To) Options on the Page tab that shrink or enlarge the printed output — either by a percentage (Adjust To) or by forcing the output to fit a set number of pages wide and tall (Fit To). Requires a printer that supports scalable/TrueType fonts.
Select Print Area→ Preview Page Breaks→ Page Setup→ Print Preview→ Print
File > Page Setup
The Page Setup dialog is the control centre for how a worksheet appears on paper — reached from File > Page Setup, or from the Page Setup button inside Print Preview.
From worksheet to printed page

Before printing, first select the range you want printed, then switch to View > Page Break Preview to see how the data will be divided across pages. If the automatic breaks fall in an awkward place, drag them or insert manual breaks. Next open File > Print, choose the correct printer, and use Page Setup to fine-tune paper size, margins, headers/footers and the sheet options. Finally check the layout in Print Preview before sending the job to the printer.
Page Setup dialog — the four tabs

c: Orientation (Portrait/Landscape), paper size, print quality, and scaling — Adjust To (%) or Fit To (pages wide by tall)
Top, bottom, left and right margin sizes; header/footer distance from the edge; Horizontally/Vertically centering checkboxes
Choosing a predefined header/footer from a dropdown, or opening Custom Header / Custom Footer to build your own

blocks.x: Orientation, paper size & scaling
Orientation

Portrait prints the page taller than it is wide (the default) and suits worksheets with many rows. Landscape prints the page wider than it is tall and suits worksheets with many columns that would otherwise be cut off.
Paper Size
Chosen from a dropdown of standard sizes (e.g. Letter, A4, Legal). Print quality (resolution, in dpi) is also set on this tab, along with the starting page number for the printout.

Adjust To vs. Fit To Adjust To scales the printout by a chosen percentage of normal size (e.g. 75%). Fit To instead lets you specify the exact number of pages wide and pages tall the printout should occupy, and the program automatically calculates the scale needed to achieve it. Both options require a printer capable of scalable/TrueType font support to render correctly at the adjusted size.
Setting page margins

The Margins tab sets the blank space around the printed data on each side of the page, and shows a live miniature preview of the page as values change. It also lets you centre the printout on the page rather than letting it print flush to the top-left corner.
Default margin values Top and Bottom: 1.0 inch | Left and Right: 0.75 inch. Header and footer margins default to a smaller distance from the page edge than the top/bottom body margins.

Center on Page checkboxes Horizontally centres the print area evenly between the left and right margins. Vertically centres it evenly between the top and bottom margins. Both can be checked together to centre the data in the middle of the page — useful for small print areas that would otherwise print in the top-left corner.
Gridlines & row/column headings

By default, the faint gridlines and the grey row-number/column-letter headings that help you navigate on screen do not print. To include them on the printed page, check the Gridlines and Row and Column Headings boxes on the Sheet tab. This is separate from whether gridlines are displayed on screen, which is toggled instead through Tools > Options > View tab (or the View ribbon's Gridlines checkbox in newer versions) and has no effect on printing.

c: Prints thin lines around every cell
Prints the 1,2,3… row numbers and A,B,C… column letters
Shows or hides gridlines only on screen; does not affect printing
Forces the printout to black-and-white even on a colour printer
Prints faster with reduced graphics/formatting quality to save ink and time

blocks.x: Page Layout Order

Down, Then Over
The default order for a print area that spans more pages than fit on one printed page in either direction. Pages are numbered down the first set of columns before moving right to the next set of columns.

Over, Then Down
The alternative order — pages are numbered across the first set of rows before moving down to the next set of rows. Choose whichever order matches how the pages will be read or assembled after printing.

sections.title: Setting and clearing the print area

blocks.x: Controlling what — and where — prints
Limiting a printout to only the needed cells, keeping header rows/columns visible on every page, and controlling exactly where one printed page ends and the next begins.
Setting and clearing the print area

Open File > Page Setup > Sheet tab and click inside the Print Area box, then either type a range reference or drag-select the desired cells directly on the worksheet. The small Collapse Dialog button (at the end of the box) shrinks the dialog out of the way so you can see and select cells more easily; clicking the Expand Dialog button (or pressing Enter) restores the full dialog once the selection is made.

Multiple print areas You can list more than one range in the Print Area box, separated by commas — e.g. A1:D10,F1:H20. Each range prints on its own page(s), in the order the ranges were entered/selected.

Print_Area — the named range Setting a print area automatically creates (or updates) a special named range called "Print_Area" for that worksheet, visible in the Name Box or Name Manager, which the program refers to whenever that sheet is printed.

Removing a print area Either delete/clear the text in the Print Area box on the Sheet tab, or use the menu shortcut File > Print Area > Clear Print Area. Once cleared, the entire used range of the worksheet becomes eligible for printing again.
Print Titles — repeating rows and columns

For a print area that spans multiple pages, the Print Titles boxes (Rows to Repeat at Top / Columns to Repeat at Left) let you choose a header row or a label column that reprints automatically on every page — so a reader flipping to page 5 can still see the column headings without scrolling back to page 1.
Vertical vs. horizontal breaks
Vertical break
Splits the printout into separate pages left to right. To insert one, place the active cell in row 1 of the column where the new page should begin, then choose Insert > Page Break.
Horizontal break
Splits the printout into separate pages top to bottom. To insert one, place the active cell in column A of the row where the new page should begin, then choose Insert > Page Break.

Both at once If the active cell is not in row 1 or column A (e.g. it sits somewhere in the middle of the sheet), Insert > Page Break inserts both a vertical break to its left and a horizontal break above it in one step.
Single break vs. all breaks

c: Click a cell just below/right of the break line, then choose Insert > Remove Page Break
Remove all manual breaks at once
Select the entire worksheet, then choose Insert > Reset All Page Breaks
View > Page Break Preview — drag the blue dashed/solid lines to move a break

items: Automatic page breaks (shown as dashed lines in Page Break Preview) are calculated by the program based on paper size, margins and scaling — they move on their own if you change those settings.
Manual page breaks (shown as solid lines) are the ones you insert yourself and stay fixed regardless of later margin or scaling changes, until you remove them.
Page Break Preview lets you drag either type of break, but dragging an automatic break converts it into a manual one.

blocks.x: Header/Footer tab & Print Preview
Adding titles, page numbers and dates to every printed page, then checking the exact final layout before committing paper and ink.
Predefined vs. custom

The Header/Footer tab of Page Setup offers a dropdown of predefined formats (e.g. "Page 1", "Sheet1", "Confidential, Page 1") that can be applied instantly. For full control, click Custom Header or Custom Footer to open a dialog with three input boxes: Left section, Center section and Right section — text and codes typed into each appear left-aligned, centred, or right-aligned on the printed page respectively.

Entering header/footer text Click directly into the Left, Center or Right box with the mouse to type free text (e.g. "CSM 177 Worksheet"), or insert dynamic codes using the toolbar buttons for page number, total pages, date, time, file name, sheet name and a picture.

Keyboard shortcuts Alt+L jumps to the Left section, Alt+C to the Center section, and Alt+R to the Right section of the Custom Header/Footer dialog. Alt+Enter inserts a line break, letting a single section hold multiple lines of header or footer text.
Checking the layout before printing

Choose File > Print Preview (or click Preview from the Print dialog) to see exactly how each page will look on paper, including margins, headers/footers, gridlines and page breaks, without using any paper.

items: 🔍Zoom in/out using the magnifying-glass pointer or the Zoom button, to check fine details like small text or borders.
▶Next/Previous buttons step through the pages of a multi-page printout one at a time.
⎙Print can be triggered directly from the preview screen once the layout looks correct.
⎋Esc (or the Close button) returns to the normal worksheet view without printing.

blocks.x: File > Print→ Select Printer→ Page Setup→ Print Preview→ Print / Esc

blocks.title: Quick checklist before printing a worksheet

items: Is the correct print area selected (not the whole, unwanted sheet)?
Do the page breaks fall in sensible places (checked in Page Break Preview)?
Is orientation (Portrait/Landscape) appropriate for the data's shape?
If the data is large, is Fit To scaling set so it doesn't spill onto extra pages awkwardly?
Do headers/footers show the right title, page numbers and date?
Have you checked the final result in Print Preview before sending it to the printer?
